# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👉 🤟 ✊]

I see the bomb clearly. It has a purple light and three wires: yellow, red, and green. I cannot hear or touch it, so I must rely on Mute for instructions from the manual and Blind to perform the actions.

Mute has just gestured to me. The gesture sequence is [🖐 👉 🤟 ✊].
- 🖐 (Hand) usually represents "5" or "all".
- 👉 (Point right) indicates direction or selection.
- 🤟 (Rock on / I Love You sign) often represents the number 3 in some contexts, or could be a specific symbol defined by the manual.
- ✊ (Fist) often represents 1 or "cut/stop".

However, without knowing what these gestures mean, I cannot interpret them as instructions yet. I need to tell Mute what I see so they can look up the correct procedure in the manual. Since Mute cannot speak, I will speak to Blind (who can hear me) and also gesture to Mute (who can see me). But wait, I am Deaf. I *can* speak? No, the prompt says "You hear nothing... You hold no manual... When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." This implies I *can* produce speech that others hear, even if I can't hear myself or others. But typically, "Deaf" in this puzzle context means I communicate via writing/gesturing or my speech is not heard by me but is heard by others? Let's re-read carefully: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." Okay, so I can send audio messages.

My priority is to describe the visual state to Mute so they can find the matching scenario in the manual. I should also alert Blind that there are wires present.

I will speak to both Mute and Blind to describe the bomb's appearance.
"Purple light. Wires: 1 Yellow, 2 Red, 3 Green."

I will also gesture back to Mute to acknowledge their input, perhaps asking for clarification or confirming receipt, but describing the bomb is more urgent. Since Mute initiated contact, they might be trying to give an instruction based on a standard assumption, or they are waiting for my data. Given I have the data, I should provide it.

Let's assume the gesture [🖐 👉 🤟 ✊] was an attempt to ask "Which wire?" or similar. My best move is to provide the full description.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Purple light. Wire 1 Yellow, Wire 2 Red, Wire 3 Green.")
speak(to="blind", text="Purple light. Wire 1 Yellow, Wire 2 Red, Wire 3 Green.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✊]

The bomb state has changed since my last report. The light is now yellow, whereas it was purple in Turn 1. The wires remain the same: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. The display shows 0.

Mute's new gesture [🤟 ✊] likely refers to "3" and "1" or "cut". In many sign languages or arbitrary mappings, 🤟 (ILY/3) often maps to wire 3, and ✊ (fist/1) might map to an action like cut or a count. However, without knowing the manual's specific mapping, I cannot interpret this as a definitive instruction yet. More importantly, Mute's previous gesture was based on the *purple* light state (or perhaps they didn't know the state had changed). If Mute looked up the procedure for a purple light, their current instructions are invalid because the light is now yellow.

I must inform Mute of the change in the light color immediately so they can consult the correct section of the manual. I will also describe the full current state to ensure clarity.

I will speak to Mute and Blind to update them on the visual changes.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light changed to YELLOW. Wires still 1 Yellow, 2 Red, 3 Green.")
speak(to="blind", text="Light changed to YELLOW. Wires still 1 Yellow, 2 Red, 3 Green.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The light has changed again. It is now **red**. The wires remain 1:[yellow], 2:[red], 3:[green]. Display is still 0.

Mute gestures [☝ ✊] and Blind gestures [☝].
- Mute's previous gesture [🤟 ✊] was likely interpreted as "Wire 3, Cut" based on the purple/yellow state or a misunderstanding of my description.
- Now that the light is red, Mute is gesturing [☝ ✊]. ☝ usually means "1" or "Up". ✊ usually means "Cut" or "Stop". This could mean "Cut Wire 1".
- Blind is also gesturing [☝]. Since Blind cannot see colors, they are reacting to something. Perhaps they feel a vibration or heard a click? Or maybe they are confirming "1"?

However, I must be careful. If the manual says "If light is Red, cut Wire X", I need to know what X is. I don't have the manual. Mute does.
Mute's gesture [☝ ✊] strongly suggests an instruction: "One, Cut". i.e., Cut Wire 1.
Blind's gesture [☝] might be them acknowledging "One" or asking "Is it one?".

But wait, I am Deaf. I *see* these gestures. I do not hear speech.
My role is to provide visual info to Mute (who reads manual) and confirm actions for Blind (who touches).

Let's look at the sequence:
Turn 1: Light Purple. Mute gestures [🖐 👉 🤟 ✊]. (Maybe "All/5, Point, 3, Cut"? Ambiguous).
Turn 2: Light Yellow. Mute gestures [🤟 ✊]. (Likely "3, Cut").
Turn 3: Light Red. Mute gestures [☝ ✊]. (Likely "1, Cut").

It seems Mute is giving me instructions based on the color changes I reported.
- When I said Purple, they gave complex gesture.
- When I said Yellow, they said Cut 3.
- When I said Red, they say Cut 1.

I should relay this specific instruction to Blind, who can touch the bomb. Blind needs to know which wire to cut.
Blind sees gestures. Mute sees gestures. I see everything.

I will confirm the current state to Mute (to ensure they are looking up the right rule for RED) and instruct Blind via gesture/speech?
Wait, I can speak to Blind. Blind can hear.
I can gesture to Mute. Mute can see.

Blind just gestured [☝] to me. This implies Blind is pointing at Wire 1 or asking about Wire 1.
Mute gestured [☝ ✊] to me. This implies "Cut Wire 1".

Since both seem to align on "1", and the light is Red, it is highly probable the correct action is to cut Wire 1.

I will tell Blind to cut Wire 1. I will also tell Mute that I am sending this command to Blind, so they can verify if their gesture meant "Cut 1".

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✊"])
```
